a large RCT was conducted in India to assess the effectiveness of different strategies for the delivery of low vision rehabilitation services.

a randomized controlled trial comparing the effectiveness of four low vision rehabilitation strategies is underway.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and evaluation of low vision rehabilitation strategies that will improve the quality of life of individuals with low vision and their families.
the effectiveness of low vision services in the context of a country with limited resources.
the effectiveness of four strategies to deliver low-vision rehabilitation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the four arms of this trial are similar in terms of their socio-demographic and visual characteristics and hence are suitable for a comparative effectiveness trial to assess the impact of different strategies of delivering low vision rehabilitation services on adaptation to age related vision loss, quality-of-life, and the effectiveness of low vision training.
the study is well designed and the sample is appropriate to the aims of the study.

the four arms of low vision rehabilitation services are comparable in terms of socio-demographic and visual characteristics of study participants and therefore, the outcomes of the trial are unlikely to be associated with differences in socio-demographic and/or vision characteristics of participants.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
center based rehabilitation is the most effective way to deliver rehabilitation services.
a mix of center-based rehabilitation with home based rehabilitation is more effective in delivering low vision rehabilitation services than center based rehabilitation alone.
the RCT is feasible, and that the socio-demographic and visual characteristics of the study participants were similar between the four arms.
The main takeaway from our work is that

low vision rehabilitation services are effective in improving the quality of life of people with vision impairment and that the mode of service delivery is not associated with the effectiveness of the intervention.
low vision rehabilitation services should not be restricted to the center but should be delivered in the home as well.
the four different models of low vision rehabilitation services are equally effective in improving adaptation to age-related low vision and quality of life.
